# Test fixture provenance

Every committed fixture has one row here. The license text of each fixture
follows the table, under a heading with the fixture's file name.

Golden vectors under `golden/` are generated, not taken from another
project. Each carries its own provenance: recipe, generator, tool versions
and tolerance. `cargo xtask golden-check` enforces it.

Pitch fixtures under `pitch/` are generated too, by this repository's own
transcriber and f0 track on generated glides, vibratos and a bass line.
Each file names its generator and carries its signal's recipe, the notes
and the track frames. The f0 track takes about half a second per second
of audio in a debug build, which adds up over the signals, so the pitch
tests read these files.
`pitch_fixtures_are_current`, an ignored test, rebuilds every file in a
release build and fails when one differs:
`cargo nextest run --release --run-ignored only -E 'test(pitch_fixtures_are_current)'`,
with `UPDATE_PITCH_FIXTURES=1` to rewrite them. MIT, like the code. The
comparison is byte for byte on the printed floats, so it holds on one
platform and toolchain; another CPU or libm can round a track frame
differently and report a fixture stale without a change in the method.
The row `pitch/*.json` gives the SHA-256 of the set's manifest,
`cd tests/fixtures/pitch && LC_ALL=C shasum -a 256 *.json | shasum -a 256`.

`cargo xtask vital-fixtures --check` fails on a file under `vital/` that the
generator does not produce, unless its origin cell starts with `saved by the
Vital app`. Such a file still needs its row, SHA-256, size and licence.

## Vital fixtures

The files under `vital/` are generated by our own code, `cargo xtask
vital-fixtures`, and fall under the project licence, MIT, as in
[LICENSE](../../LICENSE). They hold no vendor content.

## Pitch fixtures

The files under `pitch/` are generated by our own code, the ignored test
`pitch_fixtures_are_current`, from signals that `tests/it/support/pitch.rs`
and `tests/it/pitch.rs` render. They fall under the project licence, MIT,
as in [LICENSE](../../LICENSE), and hold no third-party content.
